text:
Aisha Bello: final backtest pass is done + numbers look stable. Can folks do a quick last look + sign-off on the targets so I can publish the Confluence page today?

Link (draft): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/Tiered+SLO+definitions+-+Hosted+vs+Dedicated?draft=1
Backtest notes + query diffs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1slo-backtest-q4q1

Changes since yesterday:
- Hosted streaming: split latency into TTFT + stream success, updated targets
- Dedicated: added pool readiness SLI target + clarified exclusions
- Measurement window: 28d rolling for all tier SLOs (was mixed 30d/28d)

Nadia Rahman: I re-ran the validation queries w/ the new gateway 499 mapping (client abort) + the disconnect taxonomy. The prior “streaming availability” spike was mostly misclassified 499s.

With the corrected classification:
- Hosted streaming server-side disconnect rate p50/p95 is ~0.04% / 0.12% across Q4/Q1 (excluding client abort).
- If we set target at 0.20% (28d) it’s achievable but still catches real regressions.

I’m +1 on the proposed Hosted streaming disconnect SLO target (<= 0.20%).

Sergio Costa: dashboard panels line up w/ these targets now. Only nit: can we keep the latency target naming consistent (“p95”, “p99” labels) so the alert templates don’t need special-casing.

Also confirming the backtest for latency:
- Hosted chat/completions (non-streaming): p95 e2e <= 2.8s was green in all regions except eu-west during the Jan 12 incident window (we’d have burned ~35% of monthly budget there).
- Hosted embeddings: p95 <= 450ms is green (p99 has outliers but not persistent).

Rafael Mendes: +1. The only thing I want to double-check is the windowing + exclusions text so Support doesn’t get surprised.

Specifically, for Hosted availability SLI:
- Excluding 4xx (auth/invalid request), customer-side timeouts, and explicit client abort (499)
- Including server timeouts (504) + upstream saturation (503)

That matches the draft wording now.

Allison Grant: reviewed against the org burn-rate standard doc. Targets are fine, but please keep this language in the table:
- “SLO is evaluated per tier + region + route group; per-model breakdown is for debugging, not a separate contract.”

This avoids us accidentally implying per-model SLOs where we can’t control variance.

Also, the 28d rolling choice is good (keeps burn math consistent). :thumbsup:

Amara Diallo: gateway side is good w/ the disconnect breakdown:
- `disconnect_class=client_abort` for 499 and websocket close codes we can confidently attribute to client
- `disconnect_class=server_fault` for 5xx mid-stream + runtime disconnect
- `disconnect_class=unknown` for the messy cases

Draft currently says “unknown counted as server-side” — that’s conservative and aligns w/ incentives. Works for me.

Lauren Bishop: looking at Dedicated targets now. Main question from PM side: are we comfortable w/ Dedicated availability at 99.95% (28d) given we still see a couple regions with provisioning lag spikes?

I’m okay with it if pool readiness is explicitly part of the tier and we have a separate indicator for “pool ready minutes” so customers aren’t stuck in the gray area.

Vanessa Ortiz: for Dedicated pool readiness, the SLI definition in the draft is the right framing:
- “Pool readiness = fraction of minutes in window where scheduler healthy AND capacity signal >= committed baseline AND control plane reports ready.”

Backtest shows:
- most customers are > 99.97% readiness
- the bad cases are correlated w/ autoscaler misconfig + a couple node drain events

Target at 99.90% (28d) seems achievable and gives us room to page on sustained dips without paging on every drain.

Sean Gallagher: reviewed the table + the backtest notes. This is the right set of targets for v1.

I’m explicitly signing off on:
- Hosted: Availability 99.90% (28d), non-streaming p95 latency target as written, streaming TTFT target as written, server-side disconnect <= 0.20%
- Dedicated: Availability 99.95% (28d), readiness 99.90% (28d)

Only request: add one sentence in the preamble clarifying we’ll start enforcement as “warn-only” for the first pilot services. (Targets still publish as canonical.)

Nikhil Sharma: +1 from Hosted PM side. The split between streaming TTFT vs disconnect is the right way to talk about it w/ customers.

Minor wording tweak request: can we call out that “TTFT measured at gateway from request accepted -> first token byte” (so we don’t get runtime vs gateway debates later). Otherwise good.

Aisha Bello: awesome, thanks all.

Action items I’ll do before publish:
- add preamble sentence on enforcement starting warn-only (per Sean)
- rename latency panels/targets to match standard p95/p99 labels (per Sergio)
- add explicit TTFT measurement point at gateway (per Nikhil)
- keep the “per-model is debugging” language (per Allison)

If no objections in the next ~30 mins I’m publishing + dropping link in #announcements.

Rafael Mendes: no objections. :+1:

Sergio Costa: :+1: good to publish

Lauren Bishop: :+1: ok from Dedicated

Nadia Rahman: :+1: ship it

Sean Gallagher: :shipit:
